text:
Noah Laba hasn't scored in 21 games, and the New York Post has written about the second-year forward trying to focus on the positives. A fourth-round pick in 2022 out of Colorado College, he's playing almost 15 minutes a night in a checking role, and the goals are the least of the concerns.

He has 0 goals on 2.5 expected, which is unlucky but not dramatically so. The bigger issue is the territory: the Rangers take 45% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with Laba on the ice, 11 points worse than without him, and 44% of the shot attempts. That's the profile of a young centre being asked to absorb tough minutes and not yet winning them. Our model compares him to defensive forwards like Ben Meyers and Blake Lizotte.

His value last season came mostly on the penalty kill, by Evolving-Hockey's count, and that's where he'll keep earning his ice time. Our talent range expects around 8 goals over the full season, so the first one shouldn't be far off. The thing to watch is his five-on-five share. If it doesn't rise, his minutes will probably shrink once the Rangers are healthy.
